calculus.title: Calculus — introduction to derivatives
calculus.body:
The derivative of a function f at the point x = a, written f′(a), is the limit of [f(a + h) − f(a)]/h as h → 0. This limit must exist and be a finite number.

The derivative gives the instantaneous rate of change of f at a. It is also the gradient (slope) of the tangent to the graph at that point. The fraction [f(a + h) − f(a)]/h is an average rate of change over the interval from a to a + h. As h gets smaller, this average gets closer to the instantaneous value.

For y = xⁿ, where n is a positive integer, dy/dx = nxⁿ⁻¹. The derivative of a constant is 0, because a constant does not change.

A point where the derivative is 0 is a stationary point. It is not always a maximum or a minimum: for y = x³ at x = 0, the derivative is 0, but there is neither.

Example: the displacement of a particle is s = t² metres, where t is time in seconds. Its velocity is ds/dt = 2t metres per second. At t = 3 seconds, the velocity is 6 m/s.

contrast.en: Do not confuse the average rate of change over an interval with the derivative at a point. The derivative does not exist at a sharp corner, such as y = |x| at x = 0.
contrast.ru: Не путай среднюю скорость изменения на промежутке с производной в точке. В угловой точке производной нет, например, у функции y = |x| при x = 0.

proofs.title: Mathematical proof
items: Direct proof — a chain of justified steps from the given facts to the conclusion.
Proof by contradiction — useful when a direct proof is hard, for example to show that √2 is irrational.
Proof by induction — used to prove a statement for all integers n from a starting value n₀ onwards.

Counterexample — one allowed value for which a general claim is false. One counterexample is enough to disprove the claim. For example, n = 40 disproves 'n² + n + 41 is prime for every positive integer n': 40² + 40 + 41 = 1681 = 41 × 41.

direct.name: Direct proof
direct.rule:
A direct proof starts from the premises, which are the given facts, and reaches the conclusion through valid reasoning.

For a claim 'if P, then Q', take an arbitrary object that satisfies P, and show that it satisfies Q. 'Arbitrary' means that nothing special is assumed about the object, so the result holds for every object of that kind.

This is deductive reasoning: it produces new facts from facts that are already known.
examples:
Prove that the sum of two even numbers is even.

- Let the numbers be a and b. Both are even, so a = 2m and b = 2n for some integers m and n, by the definition of an even number.
- Then a + b = 2m + 2n = 2(m + n), by the distributive law.
- The sum m + n is an integer, because the sum of two integers is always an integer.
- So a + b = 2 × (an integer), which means a + b is even, by the definition of an even number.
- Check: 4 + 6 = 2(2 + 3) = 10.

Prove that the angles of any triangle in a plane add up to 180°.

- Let the triangle be ABC. Through the vertex A, draw a line parallel to BC.
- The angle that AB makes with this line, on the side away from C, equals ∠B, because the two are alternate angles.
- The angle that AC makes with this line, on the side away from B, equals ∠C, for the same reason.
- The three angles at A lie along a straight line, so they add up to 180°.
- Therefore ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°. For example, if ∠B = 50° and ∠C = 60°, then ∠A = 70°.

Prove that a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b).

- Start with the right-hand side and expand the brackets using the distributive law: (a − b)(a + b) = a² + ab − ba − b².
- Multiplication is commutative, so ba = ab. Therefore ab − ba = 0.
- So (a − b)(a + b) = a² − b².
- The right-hand side equals the left-hand side for all values of a and b. For example, with a = 5 and b = 3, both sides equal 16.

contrast.en: Checking a few numbers does not prove a claim about all numbers. Give a reason (a definition, a rule or a theorem) for every step.
contrast.ru: Проверка нескольких чисел не доказывает утверждение обо всех числах. Для каждого шага укажи причину: определение, правило или теорему.

contradiction.name: Proof by contradiction
contradiction.rule:
To prove a statement, assume that it is false, so that its negation is true. Keep all the given conditions and the rules of logic. Then use valid steps to reach a result that cannot be true, for example 1 = 2.

The conditions and the rules of logic are true, so the added assumption must be the false part. Therefore the original statement is true.
examples:
Prove that √2 is irrational.

- Assume the opposite: √2 is rational. Then √2 = a/b, where a and b are integers with no common factor (the fraction is in its lowest terms).
- Square both sides: 2 = a²/b², so a² = 2b².
- The number a² is even, because it equals 2b². If a were odd, a² would be odd, since an odd number multiplied by itself is odd. So a is even, and we can write a = 2k, where k is an integer.
- Substitute a = 2k: (2k)² = 2b², so 4k² = 2b² and b² = 2k².
- Now b² is even, so b is even, by the same argument as for a.
- Both a and b are even, so both have a factor of 2. This contradicts the fact that a/b is in its lowest terms.
- So the assumption is false, and √2 is irrational.

Prove that there are infinitely many prime numbers.

- Assume the opposite: there are finitely many primes. Then they can be listed as p₁, p₂, …, pₙ, and this list contains all the primes.
- Let N = p₁ × p₂ × … × pₙ + 1. For example, for the primes 2, 3 and 5, N = 2 × 3 × 5 + 1 = 31.
- Divide N by any pᵢ: the remainder is 1, so no pᵢ is a factor of N.
- Every integer greater than 1 has a prime factor, because its smallest factor greater than 1 is prime. Take a prime factor of N. It cannot be any pᵢ, because no pᵢ divides N.
- This contradicts the assumption that the list contains all the primes. So there are infinitely many primes.

contrast.en: Negate carefully. The negation of 'every integer is even' is 'some integer is not even', for example 3. It is not 'no integer is even', which is false, because 2 is even.
contrast.ru: Отрицай аккуратно. Отрицание утверждения «все целые числа чётные» — это «существует целое число, которое не является чётным», например, 3. Это не «ни одно целое число не является чётным»: такое утверждение ложно, ведь 2 — чётное число.

induction.name: Proof by induction
induction.rule:
Mathematical induction proves a statement P(n) for every integer n ≥ n₀. It needs two steps.

- Base case: show that P(n₀) is true.
- Inductive step: for an arbitrary integer k ≥ n₀, assume that P(k) is true, and prove that P(k + 1) is true.

The base case starts the chain. The inductive step links each case to the next: P(n₀) gives P(n₀ + 1), which gives P(n₀ + 2), and so on for every n ≥ n₀.

Do not confuse this with inductive reasoning, which collects evidence for a pattern from examples. Mathematical induction is a deductive proof: once both steps are shown, the statement is true for every n ≥ n₀.

Example: prove that 1 + 2 + … + n = n(n + 1)/2 for every positive integer n.

- Base case: for n = 1, the left-hand side is 1, and the right-hand side is 1 × 2/2 = 1. Both sides are equal, so P(1) is true.
- Inductive step: assume 1 + 2 + … + k = k(k + 1)/2 for some integer k ≥ 1. Add k + 1 to both sides. Equal quantities stay equal when the same number is added to both.
- Factorise the right-hand side: k(k + 1)/2 + (k + 1) = (k + 1)(k/2 + 1) = (k + 1)(k + 2)/2. This is the formula with n = k + 1, so P(k + 1) is true.
- P(1) is true, and P(k) implies P(k + 1). So, by induction, the formula holds for every positive integer n.
examples:
Prove that 1 + 3 + 5 + … + (2n − 1) = n² for all positive integers n.

- Base case: when n = 1, the left-hand side is 1 and the right-hand side is 1² = 1. The statement is true for n = 1.
- Inductive hypothesis: assume that 1 + 3 + … + (2k − 1) = k² for some positive integer k.
- Add the next odd number, 2k + 1, to both sides of the hypothesis: 1 + 3 + … + (2k − 1) + (2k + 1) = k² + 2k + 1.
- Simplify the right-hand side: k² + 2k + 1 = (k + 1)², because (k + 1)² expands to k² + 2k + 1. The last term on the left is 2(k + 1) − 1, so the left-hand side is the sum for n = k + 1. Both sides equal (k + 1)², so the statement holds for k + 1.
- The statement is true for n = 1, and it is true for k + 1 whenever it is true for k. So, by induction, it is true for every positive integer n. Check: for n = 4, 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 16 = 4².

Prove that 2ⁿ > n for all positive integers n.

- Base case: when n = 1, 2¹ = 2, and 2 > 1. The statement is true for n = 1.
- Inductive hypothesis: assume that 2^k > k for some positive integer k.
- Multiply both sides of the hypothesis by 2. The inequality stays true, because 2 is positive: 2^(k + 1) > 2k.
- Since k ≥ 1, we have 2k ≥ k + 1. Therefore 2^(k + 1) > 2k ≥ k + 1.
- So the statement holds for k + 1. By induction, 2ⁿ > n for every positive integer n. Check: for n = 3, 2³ = 8 > 3.

Prove that 7ⁿ − 1 is divisible by 6 for all positive integers n.

- Base case: when n = 1, 7¹ − 1 = 6, and 6 is divisible by 6. The statement is true for n = 1.
- Inductive hypothesis: assume that 7^k − 1 is divisible by 6 for some positive integer k. Then 7^k − 1 = 6m, where m is an integer.
- Write 7^(k + 1) − 1 in terms of 7^k − 1. Expand the bracket: 7(7^k − 1) = 7 × 7^k − 7. Adding 6 gives 7(7^k − 1) + 6 = 7 × 7^k − 1 = 7^(k + 1) − 1.
- Substitute 7^k − 1 = 6m: 7^(k + 1) − 1 = 7(7^k − 1) + 6 = 7 × 6m + 6 = 6(7m + 1).
- The number 7m + 1 is an integer, so 7^(k + 1) − 1 is divisible by 6. By induction, 7ⁿ − 1 is divisible by 6 for every positive integer n. Check: for n = 2, 7² − 1 = 48 = 6 × 8.

contrast.en: Check the base case at the first value of n that the claim covers, not automatically at n = 1. For example, 2ⁿ > n² holds for every integer n ≥ 5, but it fails for n = 3, because 8 < 9. For this claim, the base case is n = 5: 2⁵ = 32 > 25.
contrast.ru: Базу индукции проверяют при первом значении n, которое входит в утверждение, а не обязательно при n = 1. Например, 2ⁿ > n² верно при всех натуральных n ≥ 5, но при n = 3 оно неверно: 8 < 9. Для этого утверждения база — n = 5: 2⁵ = 32 > 25.

counterexample.name: Counterexample
counterexample.rule:
A universal claim has the form 'for every x in a set, P(x) is true'. Any one value of x from that set for which P(x) is false refutes the claim.

For a claim 'if P, then Q', a counterexample is a case where P is true and Q is false. A case where P is false does not refute the claim, even if Q is also false.
examples: Claim: every prime number is odd. Counterexample: 2 is prime, and it is even, so the claim is false.
Claim: n² > n for every positive integer n. Counterexample: n = 1 gives 1² = 1, and the inequality 1 > 1 is false. The claim is still true for n ≥ 2, but it fails at n = 1, so it is disproved.
Claim: every quadratic equation has real roots. Counterexample: x² + 1 = 0 gives x² = −1. No real number squared is negative, so this equation has no real roots.
Claim: if a² = b², then a = b. Counterexample: take a = −3 and b = 3. Here a² = b² = 9 holds, but a = b is false, because −3 ≠ 3.

contrast.en: A value that is not in the stated set is not a counterexample. For 'n² > n for every positive integer n', the value n = 0 makes the inequality 0 > 0 false. Yet 0 is not a positive integer, so it does not count.
contrast.ru: Значение, которого нет в заданном множестве, контрпримером не является. Для утверждения «n² > n при любом целом n ≥ 1» значение n = 0 даёт неверное неравенство 0 > 0. Но 0 не удовлетворяет условию n ≥ 1, поэтому он не подходит.

numberTheory.title: Number theory basics
numberTheory.body:
A prime number is an integer greater than 1 with exactly two positive divisors: 1 and itself. For example, 7 is prime, but 9 is not, because 9 = 3 × 3.

Every integer greater than 1 can be written as primes multiplied together in only one way, apart from the order of the factors. This is called prime factorisation. For example, 60 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 2² × 3 × 5.

The difficulty of factorising very large numbers into primes underpins RSA encryption, which protects data sent online.

For integers a and b and a positive integer m, congruence modulo m is written a ≡ b (mod m) and means that m divides a − b. Equivalently, a and b leave the same remainder when divided by m. For example, 17 ≡ 2 (mod 5), because 17 − 2 = 15 is divisible by 5.

review.russianTerm: Простое число; разложение на простые множители; сравнение по модулю

contrast.en: The number 1 is neither prime nor composite. Also, 'congruence' here has nothing to do with congruent shapes, which have the same shape and size.
contrast.ru: Число 1 не бывает ни простым, ни составным (composite). Кроме того, сравнение по модулю не связано с равными фигурами, которые совпадают по форме и размеру.

complex.title: Complex numbers: a first look
complex.body:
A complex number has the form z = a + bi. Here a and b are real numbers, and i is the imaginary unit, with i² = −1. The number a is the real part of z, and b is the imaginary part. Every real number is also complex, with b = 0: for example, 5 = 5 + 0i.

Complex numbers allow solutions to equations that have no real solutions. For example, x² + 1 = 0 gives x² = −1, so x = ±i.

The square-root rule √(ab) = √a × √b does not work when both a and b are negative. For example, √(−4) × √(−9) = 2i × 3i = −6, but √((−4) × (−9)) = √36 = 6.

contrast.en: The imaginary part of 2 + 3i is 3, not 3i. The word 'imaginary' is only a name: imaginary numbers are just as valid as real numbers.
contrast.ru: Мнимая часть числа 2 + 3i равна 3, а не 3i. Слово «мнимая» — лишь название: такие числа не менее законны, чем действительные.

statsExt.title: Spread of data and correlation
statsExt.body:
Variance measures how far the values of a data set spread from the mean. For n values with mean x̄, the variance is σ² = Σ(x − x̄)² / n. Here Σ means 'add up all the values', and x is each value in turn. The standard deviation σ is the square root of the variance.

For example, the lengths 2 cm, 4 cm and 6 cm have a mean of 4 cm. The variance is (4 + 0 + 4) / 3 ≈ 2.67 cm², and the standard deviation is √2.67 ≈ 1.63 cm.

Covariance shows how x and y change together. A positive covariance means that y tends to increase as x increases, and a negative one means that y tends to decrease. The covariance depends on the units, so it is divided by σx × σy. The result is Pearson's correlation coefficient r. It has no units and always lies between −1 and 1. If r = 1, the points lie on a straight line with positive gradient. If r = −1, the line has negative gradient.

contrast.en: A correlation coefficient r = 0 means that there is no straight-line relationship. A curved relationship can still exist: for x = −2, −1, 0, 1, 2 and y = x², r = 0, although y is fully determined by x. Also, a strong correlation does not prove that one variable causes the other.
contrast.ru: Коэффициент корреляции r = 0 означает, что линейной связи нет. Криволинейная связь при этом может существовать: для x = −2, −1, 0, 1, 2 и y = x² получаем r = 0, хотя y полностью определяется значением x. Кроме того, сильная корреляция не доказывает, что одна переменная вызывает другую.

structureSets.name: Classifying numbers and notation for sets
structureSets.rule:
Each of these number sets lies inside the next one: ℕ ⊂ ℤ ⊂ ℚ ⊂ ℝ.

Here natural numbers ℕ = {1, 2, 3, …} start at 1, as in the classifier below. Integers ℤ = {…, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, …} include zero and the negative whole numbers. Rational numbers ℚ can be written as p/q, where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0. Real numbers ℝ are all the rational numbers and all the irrational numbers, such as √2.

In the notation for sets, x ∈ A means that x is one of the elements of A. A ∪ B (union) contains the elements in A or in B, and A ∩ B (intersection) contains the elements in both sets.
examples: √2 ∈ ℝ, but √2 ∉ ℚ, because √2 is an irrational number.
A recurring decimal such as 0.333… = 1/3 is rational, so 0.333… ∈ ℚ.
{x ∈ ℤ | x² < 10} means the integers x with x² < 10, so it equals {−3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3}: 3² = 9 < 10, but 4² = 16 > 10.

contrast.en: 2 ∈ ℕ means 2 is one of the numbers in ℕ, but {2} ⊆ ℕ means all the elements of {2} are in ℕ. Some books include 0 in ℕ, so state which convention you use.
contrast.ru: 2 ∈ ℕ означает, что 2 — одно из чисел в ℕ, а {2} ⊆ ℕ означает, что все элементы {2} входят в ℕ. Некоторые книги включают в ℕ ноль, поэтому укажи, какое соглашение ты используешь.

rounding.name: Rounding to decimal places and significant figures
rounding.rule: Rounding replaces a number with a nearby simpler number, to a stated degree of accuracy. You can round to a place value, such as 2 decimal places, or to a number of significant figures. Decimal places count the digits after the decimal point; significant figures count from the first non-zero digit. Look at the first digit you remove: if it is 5 or more, add 1 to the last digit you keep; if it is 0 to 4, keep that digit unchanged. Round only the final answer, not the working.
examples: 3.4567 rounded to 2 d.p. is 3.46, to 3 d.p. is 3.457, and to 2 s.f. is 3.5.
0.004532 rounded to 1 s.f. is 0.005: the first significant figure is 4, and the next digit is 5, so round up.
5400 rounded to 1 significant figure is 5000 (5 × 10³), because the next digit is 4, so the 5 stays the same.

contrast.en: The significance of trailing zeros in a whole-number measurement can be unclear unless its precision is stated. Writing 1.25 × 10³ specifies three significant figures; 1.250 × 10³ specifies four.
contrast.ru: Значимость конечных нулей в целочисленной записи результата измерения может быть неясна без указания точности. Запись 1,25 × 10³ задаёт три значащие цифры, а 1,250 × 10³ — четыре.

model.en: This rule is for positive numbers and for the convention used in this topic: an exact half is rounded up, so 2.5 rounds to 3. Some other conventions round an exact half to the nearest even whole number, which gives 2.
model.ru: Это правило относится к положительным числам и к соглашению, принятому в этой теме. Число, ровно посередине между двумя значениями, округляют вверх: 2,5 округляется до 3. В некоторых других соглашениях точную половину округляют до ближайшего чётного целого, и тогда получается 2.

bounds.name: Bounds of a rounded value (Extended)
bounds.rule: The lower bound (LB) is the smallest value that rounds to x. The upper bound (UB) is not reached: the original value can get close to it but never equal it. If a positive value v is rounded to x, to the nearest unit d, then x − d/2 ≤ v < x + d/2, where x, v and d are in the same units.
examples: A length of 27 cm, to the nearest cm, has LB = 26.5 cm and UB = 27.5 cm.
A time of 8.4 s, to 1 d.p., has LB = 8.35 s and UB = 8.45 s.

Alex measures 100 m (nearest metre) and 9.6 s (1 d.p.), so 99.5 ≤ d < 100.5 and 9.55 ≤ t < 9.65. The speed v = d/t has a lower bound of 99.5/9.65 ≈ 10.31 m/s and an upper bound of 100.5/9.55 ≈ 10.52 m/s; the speed gets close to these bounds but never reaches them.
A mass of 2.50 kg, to 3 s.f., has LB = 2.495 kg and UB = 2.505 kg.

contrast.en: Whether a bound is included depends on the rounding convention. A length of 7 cm, to the nearest centimetre, means 6.5 ≤ x < 7.5, where x is the true length, because an exact half is rounded up. Bounds cover only rounding error, not the error of the measuring instrument.
contrast.ru: Входит ли граница (bound) в промежуток, зависит от правила округления. Длина 7 см (с точностью до 1 см) означает 6,5 ≤ x < 7,5, где x — точная длина: ровно посередине округляют вверх. Такие границы учитывают только погрешность округления, но не погрешность измерительного прибора.

model.en: Let the distance s (in metres) and the time t (in seconds) be positive, with s_low ≤ s ≤ s_high and t_low ≤ t ≤ t_high, where t_low > 0. Then the lower bound of the speed s/t is s_low/t_high, and the upper bound is s_high/t_low.
model.ru: Пусть расстояние s (в метрах) и время t (в секундах) положительны, s_low ≤ s ≤ s_high и t_low ≤ t ≤ t_high, причём t_low > 0. Тогда нижняя граница (lower bound) скорости s/t равна s_low/t_high, а верхняя — s_high/t_low.

exponents.name: Laws of exponents
exponents.rule: For a positive integer n, aⁿ means n factors of a multiplied together. So aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ, because there are m + n factors of a. For a ≠ 0, the quotient rule gives aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ, and the power rule gives (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ. The power of products rule gives (ab)ⁿ = aⁿbⁿ. The zero power rule gives a⁰ = 1, and the negative power rule gives a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ, both for a ≠ 0.
examples: (2x³)² = 4x⁶.

contrast.en: You cannot add exponents when the bases differ: 2³ × 3⁴ is not 6⁷. A power of a sum is not the sum of the powers: (2 + 3)² = 25, not 2² + 3² = 13.
contrast.ru: При умножении степеней с разными основаниями показатели складывать нельзя: 2³ · 3⁴ не равно 6⁷. Степень суммы не равна сумме степеней: (2 + 3)² = 25, а не 2² + 3² = 13.

fractionalIndices.name: Writing roots as fractional indices (Extended)
fractionalIndices.rule: For a > 0 and integers m and n with n > 0, a^(m/n) = (ⁿ√a)ᵐ. The denominator n gives the root, and the numerator m gives the power. The nth root of a is the positive number whose nth power is a. If m is negative, take the reciprocal of the result.
examples: The side of a square with area 36 cm² is 36^(1/2) = √36 = 6 cm.

contrast.en: The symbol √9 gives only the principal (positive) square root, 3. The equation x² = 9, however, has two solutions: x = 3 and x = −3.
contrast.ru: Знак √9 обозначает только арифметический квадратный корень (principal square root), то есть 3. А уравнение x² = 9 имеет два решения: x = 3 и x = −3.

model.en: The rule above is for a > 0. Even roots of negative numbers are not real: √(−4) does not exist. Odd roots do exist, for example ∛(−8) = −2.
model.ru: Правило выше верно при a > 0. Корни чётной степени из отрицательных чисел не существуют в действительных числах, например √(−4). Корни нечётной степени существуют, например ∛(−8) = −2.

standardForm.name: Standard form (scientific notation)
standardForm.rule: Standard form, or scientific notation, writes a non-zero number as a × 10ⁿ, where n is an integer and 1 ≤ |a| < 10. The coefficient a carries the significant figures. The power of ten, n, shows how far the decimal point moves: to the right if n is positive, to the left if n is negative. Zero has no standard form; it is written simply as 0.
examples: The speed of light is about 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s, or 300,000,000 m/s.

contrast.en: 54 × 10⁴ and 5.4 × 10⁵ are equal, but only 5.4 × 10⁵ is in standard form, because 5.4 lies between 1 and 10. In algebra, standard form means ax² + bx + c for a quadratic function.
contrast.ru: 54 × 10⁴ и 5,4 × 10⁵ равны. Но стандартный вид числа — только вторая запись, потому что коэффициент 5,4 лежит между 1 и 10. В алгебре «стандартным видом» называют запись квадратичной функции: ax² + bx + c.

unitConversion.name: Converting units of length, area, volume and speed
unitConversion.rule: Converting units changes the unit of measurement, but not the quantity. Multiply by a conversion factor equal to 1, such as 1000 m / 1 km = 1. For area, square the conversion factor; for volume, cube it. For a compound unit such as speed in m/s, convert the numerator and the denominator separately.
examples: 72 km/h = 72 × 1000 m / 3600 s = 20 m/s. A shortcut is to divide by 3.6, because 1 m/s = 3.6 km/h.
2.5 hours = 2.5 × 60 × 60 s = 9000 s. One hour has 60 minutes, and each minute has 60 seconds.
A 0.5-litre bottle holds 500 cm³, because 0.5 × 1000 = 500 and 1 litre = 1000 cm³.

contrast.en: A common mistake is to forget to square the 100: 1 m = 100 cm, so 1 m² = (100 cm)² = 10 000 cm², not 100 cm².
contrast.ru: Частая ошибка — забыть возвести в квадрат число 100: 1 м = 100 см, поэтому 1 м² = (100 см)² = 10 000 см², а не 100 см².

surdsSimplify.name: Writing a surd in simplest form
surdsSimplify.rule: A surd is a square root with an irrational value, such as √2 or √12. The square root of a positive whole number that is not a perfect square is always a surd. To simplify a surd, take out a square factor: √(a²b) = |a|√b for real a and b ≥ 0.
examples: √(8x²) = 2|x|√2 for real x. When x = −1, the result is 2√2, not −2√2, because the square root sign means the positive root.

contrast.en: √9 = 3 is written with a root sign, but its value is rational, so it is not a surd. π is irrational, but it is not the square root of a rational number, so it is not a surd either.
contrast.ru: √9 = 3 записано со знаком корня, но значение рационально, поэтому это не иррациональный корень. Число π иррационально, но оно не является корнем из рационального числа, поэтому тоже не иррациональный корень.

surdsOperate.name: Operations with surds and rationalising the denominator
surdsOperate.rule:
Multiplying and dividing: combine two roots under one root sign, √a × √b = √(ab) and √a/√b = √(a/b), for a ≥ 0 and b > 0.

Adding and subtracting: only like surds can be combined, that is, surds with the same number under the root: p√d + q√d = (p + q)√d.

Rationalising the denominator: rewrite a fraction with a surd in the denominator as an equal fraction with a rational denominator. Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same nonzero expression, often the conjugate, which has the opposite sign between its two terms.
examples: (2 + √5)(2 − √5) = 2² − (√5)² = 4 − 5 = −1, a difference of squares
5/√2 = (5 × √2)/(√2 × √2) = 5√2/2, multiplying the numerator and the denominator by √2

contrast.en: A root of a sum is not the sum of the roots: √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5, but √9 + √16 = 3 + 4 = 7.
contrast.ru: Корень из суммы не равен сумме корней: √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5, а √9 + √16 = 3 + 4 = 7.

absolute.name: How far is a number from zero?
absolute.rule: The absolute value of a number is its distance from 0 on the number line, written |x|. For a real number x: |x| = x if x ≥ 0, and |x| = −x if x < 0. It can also be written as |x| = √(x²). So |x| is never negative.
examples: |3 − 10| = |−7| = 7, the distance from 3 to 10
|x − 5| = 3 means x − 5 = 3 or x − 5 = −3, so x = 8 or x = 2

contrast.en: The absolute value of a difference is not the difference of absolute values: |2 − 9| = |−7| = 7, but |2| − |9| = 2 − 9 = −7.
contrast.ru: Модуль разности не равен разности модулей: |2 − 9| = |−7| = 7, а |2| − |9| = 2 − 9 = −7.

functionsAlgebra.title: Functions & Algebra
functionsAlgebra.intro: This page covers mappings, domain and range, quadratic expressions, quadratic functions and their graphs, and transformations of graphs. Then come solving quadratic equations, rearranging formulae, algebraic fractions, proportion, asymptotes and exponential functions.

mappings.name: Mappings, domain and range
mappings.rule: A mapping pairs each element of one set with an element of another set. A function is a mapping in which each input has exactly one output. The domain is the set of input values; the range is the set of output values the function actually produces.
examples: f(x) = x², domain ℝ, range [0, ∞).
g(x) = 1/x, domain ℝ \ {0}, range ℝ \ {0}.
h(x) = √x, domain [0, ∞), range [0, ∞).
If f(x) = 3x − 2, then f(4) = 10 and f(−1) = −5.

contrast.en: Do not mix up the domain (the allowed inputs) with the range (the outputs that actually occur). Exam tip: when you are asked for the range, write outputs, not inputs.
contrast.ru: Не путай область определения (допустимые аргументы) и область значений (значения, которые функция действительно даёт). Если на экзамене спрашивают область значений, пиши значения функции, а не аргументы.

sources.title: Фоксфорд Учебник — Понятие функции и способы её задания
Oscar Levin — 5.2 Functions — Domain, Codomain and Range

caption.en: Put −2, 0 and 2 into the rule. The outputs are 4, 0 and 4, so the range for these inputs is {0, 4}.
caption.ru: Подставь −2, 0 и 2 в правило. Получаются значения 4, 0 и 4, значит, область значений для этих аргументов — {0, 4}.

verticalLine.name: Vertical line test: when a graph is a function
verticalLine.rule: A graph shows y as a function of x if every vertical line crosses it at most once. If a vertical line crosses the graph two or more times, one x-value gives two or more y-values, so the graph is not a function.
examples: y = x² is a function: every vertical line crosses its parabola at most once.
x = y² is not a function: the vertical line x = 1 meets the graph at y = 1 and y = −1.
The circle x² + y² = 4 is not a function. The vertical line x = 0 crosses it at y = 2 and at y = −2.

contrast.en: Do not confuse many-to-one with one-to-many. Several x-values can share one y-value, as in y = x²: x = √5 and x = −√5 (≈ ±2.24) both give y = 5, and this is allowed. One x-value giving two y-values is not allowed, as in y² = x: x = 4 gives y = 2 and y = −2.
contrast.ru: Не путай два случая: несколько значений x могут давать одно значение y, а один x — два значения y. В y = x² при x = √5 и x = −√5 (≈ ±2,24) получаем y = 5, и это допустимо для функции. В y² = x один x даёт два значения y: при x = 4 получаем y = 2 и y = −2, и это уже не функция.

sources.title: Фоксфорд Учебник — Понятие функции и способы её задания

quadraticsFactor.name: Expanding and factorising quadratic expressions
quadraticsFactor.rule: A quadratic expression has the form ax² + bx + c, where a ≠ 0. Expanding removes brackets: multiply every term in one bracket by every term in the other. Factorising does the reverse: it writes the expression as brackets multiplied together. Do not mix up the two words: terms are added (x², 7x, 12), but factors are multiplied, as in (x + 3)(x + 4).
examples: Expand: (x + 3)(x − 5) = x² − 2x − 15.
Factorise: x² + 7x + 12 = (x + 3)(x + 4), because 3 × 4 = 12 and 3 + 4 = 7.
Factorise: x² − 5x − 14 = (x − 7)(x + 2), because −7 × 2 = −14 and −7 + 2 = −5.
Difference of squares: x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3).
Leading coefficient 2: 2x² + 7x + 3 = (2x + 1)(x + 3). Check the middle term: 2 × 3 + 1 × 1 = 7, and the constant term: 1 × 3 = 3.

contrast.en: Do not confuse factorising with solving. (x + 3)(x + 4) is an expression, but (x + 3)(x + 4) = 0 is an equation. For x² + bx + c = (x + p)(x + q), you need p + q = b and pq = c. Some quadratic expressions cannot be factorised using whole numbers.
contrast.ru: Не путай разложение с решением. (x + 3)(x + 4) — это выражение, а (x + 3)(x + 4) = 0 — уравнение. Для x² + bx + c = (x + p)(x + q) нужно, чтобы p + q = b и pq = c. Некоторые квадратные выражения нельзя разложить на множители с целыми числами.

caption.en: The first two expressions are equal for every x. Setting (x + 3)(x + 4) equal to 0 gives an equation with two solutions.
caption.ru: Первые два выражения равны при любом x. Если приравнять (x + 3)(x + 4) к нулю, получится уравнение с двумя решениями.

quadraticsGraph.name: Quadratic graphs: the parabola, its intercepts and its vertex
quadraticsGraph.rule: A quadratic function f(x) = ax² + bx + c, where a ≠ 0, has a parabola as its graph. The parabola crosses the y-axis at (0, c). Its x-intercepts are the points where f(x) = 0. The vertex is the lowest point if a > 0, and the highest point if a < 0. Its x-coordinate is −b/(2a).
examples: y = x² − 4x + 3 opens upwards. It crosses the y-axis at (0, 3) and the x-axis at x = 1 and x = 3.
y = −x² + 4 opens downwards. It crosses the y-axis at (0, 4) and the x-axis at x = −2 and x = 2.
For y = −x² + 2x + 3, x = −b/(2a) = −2/(2 × (−1)) = 1. Then y = −1 + 2 + 3 = 4, so the vertex is (1, 4). It is a maximum, because a = −1 is negative.

contrast.en: Do not confuse a root with an intercept. A root is an x-value, for example x = 2. An x-intercept is a point, for example (2, 0). A double root means the parabola touches the x-axis at its vertex without crossing it.
contrast.ru: Не путай корень и точку пересечения. Корень — это значение x, например x = 2. Точка пересечения с осью x — это точка (2; 0). Двойной корень означает, что парабола касается оси x в вершине и не пересекает её.

vertexForm.name: Vertex form: the vertex, the axis of symmetry and completing the square
vertexForm.rule: The vertex form is y = a(x − h)² + k, where a ≠ 0. The vertex is the point (h, k), and the axis of symmetry is the line x = h. The value k is the minimum of y if a > 0, and the maximum if a < 0. Completing the square changes ax² + bx + c into this form without changing its values.
examples: Complete the square: x² − 6x + 5 = (x − 3)² − 4, so the vertex is (3, −4).
For y = 2x² + 8x − 3, take 2 out of the first two terms: y = 2(x² + 4x) − 3. Complete the square inside the bracket: y = 2[(x + 2)² − 4] − 3 = 2(x + 2)² − 11. So the vertex is (−2, −11).

contrast.en: Watch the sign. In (x + 2)², the value of h is −2, because the bracket is (x − h). If a ≠ 1, take a out of the x² and x terms first, and leave the constant term outside the bracket.
contrast.ru: Смотри на знак. В (x + 2)² значение h равно −2, потому что в скобке стоит x − h. Если a ≠ 1, сначала вынеси a только из членов с x² и x, а свободный член оставь за скобками.

transformations.name: Transformations of graphs: shifts, stretches and reflections
transformations.rule:
A transformation changes the position or the shape of a graph. In y = a f(x − h) + k, h shifts the graph right by h units, and k shifts it up by k units. If h or k is negative, the shift goes the opposite way. The value |a| is the vertical stretch factor, and a negative a also reflects the graph in the x-axis.

Extended: for y = f(bx), the graph is stretched horizontally by the factor 1/|b|, and a negative b reflects it in the y-axis.
examples: y = (x − 3)² + 2 is the graph of y = x² moved 3 units right and 2 units up. Its vertex is (3, 2).
y = 2x² is the graph of y = x² stretched vertically by factor 2: every y-value doubles. For example, when x = 1, y changes from 1 to 2.

Extended: y = (2x)² = 4x². For y = x², a horizontal scale factor of 1/2 gives the same graph as a vertical stretch by factor 4. For y = x³, the same horizontal factor gives a vertical stretch by factor 8, so the vertical factor depends on the function.
y = −x² is the graph of y = x² reflected in the x-axis. The point (2, 4) on y = x² moves to (2, −4).

contrast.en: f(2x) compresses the graph horizontally: every horizontal distance is halved, so the horizontal scale factor is 1/2. The order of stretching and shifting matters, because doing them in a different order can give a different graph.
contrast.ru: f(2x) сжимает график по горизонтали: все горизонтальные расстояния уменьшаются вдвое, поэтому коэффициент растяжения по горизонтали равен 1/2. Порядок растяжения и сдвига важен: в другом порядке эти действия могут дать другой график.

solveGeneral.name: Quadratic equations and their real roots
solveGeneral.rule: An equation is a statement that two expressions are equal. A solution is a value of the variable that makes the equation true. A quadratic equation can be written as ax² + bx + c = 0, where a ≠ 0. The discriminant, Δ = b² − 4ac, shows how many real roots there are: two distinct roots if Δ > 0, one repeated root if Δ = 0, and no real roots if Δ < 0.
examples: x² − 4x + 4 = 0: Δ = (−4)² − 4 × 1 × 4 = 0, so there is one repeated root, x = 2.
x² + x + 1 = 0: Δ = 1² − 4 × 1 × 1 = −3 < 0, so there are no real solutions.

contrast.en: You simplify or factorise an expression, but you solve an equation to find the values of x.
contrast.ru: Выражение упрощают или раскладывают на множители, а уравнение решают, чтобы найти значения x.

solveFactor.name: Solving quadratic equations by factorising
solveFactor.rule: If two numbers multiply to give zero, at least one of them is zero. First move all the terms to one side, so that the other side is zero, then factorise the expression. Then set each bracket equal to zero and solve: if (x − p)(x − q) = 0, then x = p or x = q.
examples: x² + 2x = 0: take out the common factor x to get x(x + 2) = 0, so x = 0 or x = −2.
x² = 16: subtract 16 to get x² − 16 = 0, so (x − 4)(x + 4) = 0 and x = 4 or x = −4.

contrast.en: This rule works only when the brackets multiply to give zero: in (x − 2)(x − 3) = 5, you cannot set each bracket equal to 5. Dividing both sides of x² = 3x by x loses the solution x = 0.
contrast.ru: Это правило работает только тогда, когда произведение равно нулю: в (x − 2)(x − 3) = 5 нельзя приравнять каждую скобку к 5. Деление обеих частей x² = 3x на x теряет решение x = 0.

solveCompleteSquare.name: Solving quadratic equations by completing the square
solveCompleteSquare.rule: Completing the square rewrites x² + 2px as (x + p)² − p². Isolate the squared bracket to get (x + p)² = q. If q ≥ 0, the solutions are x = −p ± √q; if q < 0, there are no real solutions. When the equation has the form ax² + bx + c = 0, first divide every term by a, where a ≠ 0.
examples: x² + 6x − 7 = 0: (x + 3)² − 9 − 7 = 0, so (x + 3)² = 16 and x + 3 = ±4. Therefore x = 1 or x = −7.

contrast.en: The symbol √q gives only the non-negative root, so the ± sign is needed. For example, both 4 and −4 square to 16.
contrast.ru: Символ √q обозначает только неотрицательный корень, поэтому нужен знак ±. Например, и 4, и −4 при возведении в квадрат дают 16.

solveFormula.name: Solving quadratic equations with the quadratic formula
solveFormula.rule: For a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, with a ≠ 0, the quadratic formula gives the solutions x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / (2a). The part under the square root, Δ = b² − 4ac, is the discriminant. If Δ ≥ 0, the formula gives real solutions; if Δ < 0, there are no real solutions. Divide the whole numerator by 2a, and take care with signs: if b = −5, then −b = 5.

contrast.en: An exact answer can contain a square root, such as (5 ± √17) / 4. Write a decimal approximation with ≈ and round only the final answer.
contrast.ru: Точный ответ может содержать квадратный корень, например (5 ± √17) / 4. Приближённое значение пиши со знаком ≈ и округляй только итоговый ответ.

solveGraphical.name: Solving equations graphically
solveGraphical.rule: A solution of f(x) = 0 is an x-value where the graph of y = f(x) crosses or touches the x-axis. A solution of f(x) = g(x) is an x-value where the graphs of y = f(x) and y = g(x) meet. If the graph only touches the x-axis, that point is still a solution, called a repeated root.
examples: To solve x² − 4 = 0, plot y = x² − 4. It crosses the x-axis at x = −2 and x = 2.
To solve x² = x + 2, plot y = x² and y = x + 2. The graphs meet at two points, where x = −1 and x = 2, so these are the solutions.

contrast.en: A graph gives an estimate, not an exact answer. Check your answer by substituting it into the equation. A viewing window that is too small can hide a solution.
contrast.ru: График даёт приближённый ответ, а не точный. Проверь ответ, подставив его в уравнение. Слишком маленькое окно графика может скрыть решение.

rearrange.name: Rearranging a formula to make a chosen variable the subject
rearrange.rule: A formula is an equation that shows how quantities are related. Changing the subject means rearranging the formula so that one chosen variable is on its own on one side. Do the same operation to both sides, and check that you never divide by zero. After you take a square root, choose the sign using the context of the problem.
examples: Make r the subject of A = πr²: r² = A/π, so r = √(A/π). A radius is positive, so take the positive root. For A = 50 cm², r ≈ 3.99 cm.
Make t the subject of v = u + at. Subtract u from both sides: v − u = at. Divide both sides by a (a ≠ 0): t = (v − u)/a. Check with v = 20 m/s, u = 5 m/s and a = 3 m/s²: t = (20 − 5)/3 = 5 s.
Make h the subject of V = πr²h/3. Multiply both sides by 3: 3V = πr²h. Divide by πr² (r ≠ 0): h = 3V/(πr²). Check with r = 2 cm and V = 8π cm³: h = 3 × 8π/(π × 2²) = 6 cm.

Make x the subject of y = (x + 1)/(x − 2), where x ≠ 2. Multiply both sides by (x − 2): y(x − 2) = x + 1. Expand: yx − 2y = x + 1. Move the x terms to the left: yx − x = 2y + 1. Take x outside the brackets: x(y − 1) = 2y + 1, so x = (2y + 1)/(y − 1), where y ≠ 1. Check with y = 2: x = 5, and (5 + 1)/(5 − 2) = 2.

contrast.en: A radius cannot be negative, so from A = πr² we get r = √(A/π), not ±√(A/π). From v = u + at, t = (v − u)/a only when a ≠ 0.
contrast.ru: Радиус не может быть отрицательным, поэтому из A = πr² получаем r = √(A/π), а не ±√(A/π). Из v = u + at получаем t = (v − u)/a только при a ≠ 0.

algebraicFractions.name: Simplifying algebraic fractions; Extended: solving equations with them
algebraicFractions.rule:
An algebraic fraction (rational algebraic expression) is one algebraic expression divided by another. It is undefined when its denominator is zero, so state the values that are not allowed, for example x ≠ 0. Add fractions over a common denominator, multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators, and divide by multiplying by the reciprocal. Factorise first, then cancel common factors; cancelling does not remove the restrictions on the variable.

Extended: when you multiply both sides of an equation by an expression that contains the variable, check every solution in the original equation.
examples: Solve 3/(x − 1) + 2/(x + 1) = 1, where x ≠ 1 and x ≠ −1. Multiply both sides by (x − 1)(x + 1): 3(x + 1) + 2(x − 1) = (x − 1)(x + 1). This gives 5x + 1 = x² − 1, so x² − 5x − 2 = 0. Then x = (5 ± √33)/2, so x ≈ 5.37 or x ≈ −0.37. Both values are allowed.

contrast.en: Cancel common factors, not terms. (x² − 9)/(x − 3) = x + 3 for x ≠ 3, but in (x + 1)/x the x cannot be cancelled, because x is not a factor of the whole numerator (x + 1).
contrast.ru: Сокращай общие множители, а не слагаемые. (x² − 9)/(x − 3) = x + 3 при x ≠ 3, но в (x + 1)/x сокращать x нельзя: это не множитель всего числителя (x + 1).

proportions.name: Direct and inverse proportion: y = kx and y = k/x
proportions.rule: Two quantities are directly proportional if y = kx, where k is a non-zero constant called the constant of proportionality. Then y/x = k for every x ≠ 0, and the graph is a straight line through the origin. Two quantities are inversely proportional if y = k/x, so xy = k. Doubling x halves y. To find k, substitute one known pair of values. If y is proportional to x², then y = kx².
examples: Cost is directly proportional to weight. If 3 kg cost £6, then k = 6 ÷ 3 = £2 per kg. So 5 kg cost 2 × 5 = £10.
Time is inversely proportional to speed for a fixed distance. At 60 km/h a trip takes 4 hours, so the distance is k = 60 × 4 = 240 km. At 80 km/h the time is 240 ÷ 80 = 3 hours.

The area of a circle is directly proportional to the square of its radius: A = πr², so k = π. With r = 2 cm, A = 4π ≈ 12.6 cm². With r = 4 cm, A = 16π ≈ 50.3 cm². Doubling the radius makes the area four times bigger.
4 people finish a job in 6 days, so k = 4 × 6 = 24 person-days. With 8 people, the job takes 24 ÷ 8 = 3 days.

contrast.en: The line y = mx + c with c ≠ 0 is not direct proportion, because it does not pass through the origin. A decreasing graph is not automatically inverse proportion: y must equal k/x.
contrast.ru: График y = mx + c при c ≠ 0 — это не прямая пропорциональность: он не проходит через начало координат. Убывающий график ещё не означает обратную пропорциональность: y должен равняться k/x.

asymptotes.name: Extended: asymptotes of rational functions
asymptotes.rule: An asymptote is a line that a graph gets closer and closer to. A vertical asymptote is at x = c, where the denominator is zero and the factor does not cancel. A horizontal asymptote y = L shows the value the function approaches as |x| becomes very large. For f(x) = a/(x − h) + k, with a ≠ 0, the asymptotes are x = h and y = k.
examples: y = 1/(x − 3): the vertical asymptote is x = 3, because the denominator is zero there. The horizontal asymptote is y = 0. For example, y = 1 when x = 4.
y = (x + 1)/(x − 2) = 1 + 3/(x − 2). The vertical asymptote is x = 2, and the horizontal asymptote is y = 1. Check with x = 5: (5 + 1)/(5 − 2) = 2 and 1 + 3/3 = 2.
y = 1/x²: the vertical asymptote is x = 0 and the horizontal asymptote is y = 0. Unlike y = 1/x, the graph stays above the x-axis, because x² is always greater than zero when x ≠ 0.

contrast.en: If a zero of the denominator cancels, the graph has a hole, not an asymptote. For (x² − 4)/(x − 2), the hole is at (2, 4). A graph can cross its horizontal asymptote.
contrast.ru: Если ноль знаменателя сокращается, на графике будет выколотая точка, а не асимптота. У (x² − 4)/(x − 2) выколота точка (2; 4). График может пересекать горизонтальную асимптоту.

exponential.name: Extended: exponential functions — growth and decay
exponential.rule: An exponential function has the form y = A·bˣ, where A is the starting value and b is the constant growth factor (A > 0, b > 0, b ≠ 1). Each time x increases by 1, y is multiplied by b. The graph passes through (0, A). If b > 1, the function shows growth. If 0 < b < 1, it shows decay.
examples: y = 2ˣ: each time x increases by 1, y doubles. Check: y(0) = 1, y(1) = 2 and y(3) = 8.
A laptop is worth £100 and loses 10% of its value each year, so V = 100 × 0.9ᵗ, where t is the number of years. After 1 year V = £90, and after 2 years V = £81.
Compound interest: A = P(1 + r)ⁿ, where P is the starting sum, r is the yearly rate as a decimal and n is the number of years. For £500 at 4% a year for 3 years: A = 500 × 1.04³ ≈ £562.43.

Bacteria: N = N₀ × 2⁽ᵗ/ᵀ⁾, where N₀ is the starting number, t is the time in hours and T is the doubling time. A colony starts with 100 cells and doubles every 3 hours. After 6 hours: N = 100 × 2⁽⁶/³⁾ = 100 × 2² = 400 cells.

contrast.en: In bˣ the variable is the power, not the base. In x² the variable is the base: at x = 1, 2, 3 the values are 1, 4 and 9, and the ratio between steps is not fixed. A fixed percentage change is not the same as a fixed amount added each time.
contrast.ru: В bˣ переменная стоит в показателе, а не в основании. В x² переменная — основание: при x = 1, 2, 3 значения равны 1, 4 и 9, и множитель между шагами не постоянен. Постоянный процентный рост не совпадает с постоянной прибавкой.

model.en: A fixed growth rate is a modelling assumption. Populations cannot keep the same rate of growth indefinitely, because resources are limited.
model.ru: Постоянный темп роста — это допущение модели. Численность населения не может расти с одним и тем же темпом неограниченно долго: ресурсы ограничены.

sequences.title: Sequences & Series
sequences.intro: Arithmetic sequences: the rule for the nth term and the sum of the first n terms. Extended: geometric sequences: the rule for the nth term, and the sum to infinity of a geometric series.

linearGeneral.name: Arithmetic sequences: recursive and explicit formulas
linearGeneral.rule:
An arithmetic sequence is a sequence in which the difference between consecutive terms is constant. This constant is the common difference, d.

With first term u₁, the recursive formula is uₙ₊₁ = uₙ + d, so each term is the previous term plus d. The explicit formula gives any term directly: uₙ = u₁ + (n − 1)d, where u₁ is the first term and n is the term number, a positive whole number.

The graph of an arithmetic sequence is a set of separate points on a straight line, because n takes only whole-number values.
examples: Using uₙ = 23 − 3n for the sequence 20, 17, 14, …, the 10th term is u₁₀ = 23 − 30 = −7.
What is the 100th term of 7, 12, 17, …? Here u₁ = 7 and d = 5, so u₁₀₀ = 7 + 99 × 5 = 502.

contrast.en: A term is one value: u₄ = 11 in 2, 5, 8, 11. A sum adds several terms: the sum of the first four terms is 2 + 5 + 8 + 11 = 26.
contrast.ru: Член — одно значение: u₄ = 11 в последовательности 2, 5, 8, 11. Сумма — результат сложения нескольких членов: сумма первых четырёх членов равна 2 + 5 + 8 + 11 = 26.

linearProblems.name: Solving problems with arithmetic sequences: u₁, d and the term number
linearProblems.rule:
Two known terms give the common difference. If uₚ and u_q are known, then u_q − uₚ = (q − p)d, so d = (u_q − uₚ) ÷ (q − p) when p ≠ q. Then use uₚ = u₁ + (p − 1)d to find u₁.

To check whether a value occurs in the sequence, solve u₁ + (n − 1)d = value for n. The value occurs only if n is a positive whole number.
examples: The 5th term is 22 and the 10th term is 47. Find u₁ and d. Since u₁₀ − u₅ = 5d, we get 47 − 22 = 5d, so d = 5. Then u₁ = u₅ − 4d = 22 − 4 × 5 = 2.
Is 200 a term of 3, 7, 11, …? Here u₁ = 3 and d = 4. From 200 = 3 + 4(n − 1) we get 4(n − 1) = 197, so n − 1 = 49.25 and n = 50.25. The term number must be a whole number, so 200 is not a term.
Let S₂₀ be the sum of the first 20 terms of 2, 5, 8, …. Use Sₙ = n(u₁ + uₙ) ÷ 2. Here u₁ = 2, d = 3 and u₂₀ = 2 + 19 × 3 = 59, so S₂₀ = 20 × (2 + 59) ÷ 2 = 610.

contrast.en: Do not take the difference between any two terms as d. The difference u₈ − u₃ equals 5d, because there are 5 steps from the 3rd term to the 8th.
contrast.ru: Не принимай разность любых двух членов за d. Разность u₈ − u₃ равна 5d: от 3-го члена до 8-го — 5 шагов.

geometric.name: Extended: geometric sequences: the common ratio and the nth term
geometric.rule:
Extended: a geometric sequence is a sequence in which the ratio between consecutive terms is constant. This constant is the common ratio, r, so each term is r times the previous term.

With first term u₁, the recursive formula is uₙ₊₁ = r uₙ. The explicit formula is uₙ = u₁rⁿ⁻¹, where n is the term number, a positive whole number. The common ratio cannot be 0, and you cannot divide by a term that is 0 when you find r.
examples: £500 invested at 4% per year: 500, 520, 540.8, …, so r = 1.04. After n years the amount is 500 × 1.04ⁿ, where n = 0 is the starting amount.

contrast.en: Compare with the arithmetic case, where the terms change by a fixed amount d. Here they change by a fixed factor r, so check r first. If −1 < r < 1, the terms get closer to 0. If r > 1 or r < −1, their size grows. If r < 0, the signs alternate.
contrast.ru: Сравни с арифметической прогрессией. Там члены меняются на одну и ту же величину d. Здесь они умножаются на один и тот же множитель r, поэтому сначала проверь r. Если −1 < r < 1, члены приближаются к 0. Если r > 1 или r < −1, их модули растут. Если r < 0, знаки чередуются.

sumInfinity.name: Extended: sum to infinity of a geometric series
sumInfinity.rule:
A series is the sum of the terms of a sequence.

Extended: the sum to infinity, S∞, is the value that the sums of the first n terms approach as n grows. If the first term u₁ is not 0, S∞ exists only when −1 < r < 1. Then S∞ = u₁ ÷ (1 − r).
examples: The recurring decimal 0.111… = 0.1 + 0.01 + 0.001 + …, with u₁ = 0.1 and r = 0.1. So S∞ = 0.1 ÷ 0.9 = 1/9.

contrast.en: Do not use the formula when |r| ≥ 1. For 1 − 1 + 1 − 1 + … (r = −1) the formula would give 1 ÷ 2 = 0.5, but the partial sums 1, 0, 1, 0, … do not settle, so there is no sum to infinity. For r = 1 the formula divides by 0.
contrast.ru: Формулу нельзя применять при |r| ≥ 1. Для 1 − 1 + 1 − 1 + … (r = −1) формула дала бы 1 : 2 = 0,5, но частичные суммы 1, 0, 1, 0, … не приближаются к одному числу, значит, бесконечной суммы нет. При r = 1 в формуле получается деление на 0.

geometryTrig.title: Geometry & Trigonometry
geometryTrig.intro: This page covers right-angled triangles, bearings and circles, plus Extended rules for other triangles. Pythagoras and the trigonometric ratios work only in right-angled triangles. Parts marked Extended are higher-level content: the converse of Pythagoras, the sine and cosine rules and the area formula ½ab sin C.

pythagoras.name: Pythagoras’ theorem
pythagoras.rule:
In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides: a² + b² = c². Here a and b are the legs, the sides that meet at the right angle. The hypotenuse c is opposite the right angle and is always the longest side.

Extended: the converse is also true. If the sides of a triangle satisfy a² + b² = c², where c is the longest side, then the angle opposite c is 90°.

In the exam, first decide whether you are finding the hypotenuse or a leg. Add the squares of the legs to find the hypotenuse, and subtract the square of the known leg from the square of the hypotenuse to find a leg.
examples: Legs 3 cm and 4 cm: hypotenuse c = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 cm.
Hypotenuse 13 cm and one leg 5 cm: the other leg is b = √(13² − 5²) = √144 = 12 cm.
Extended: is a triangle with sides 7 cm, 24 cm and 25 cm right-angled? 7² + 24² = 49 + 576 = 625 = 25², so yes.
A 5 m ladder stands against a wall with its foot 3 m from the wall. The top of the ladder reaches a height h on the wall: h = √(5² − 3²) = √16 = 4 m.

contrast.en: Pythagoras works only when the triangle has a right angle. If there is no right angle, a² + b² = c² does not work, so use the cosine rule (Extended) instead.
contrast.ru: Теорема Пифагора работает только тогда, когда в треугольнике есть прямой угол. Если прямого угла нет, формула a² + b² = c² не работает, поэтому используй теорему косинусов (Extended).

trig.name: Sine, cosine and tangent of an acute angle
trig.rule:
Take an acute angle θ in a right-angled triangle. The hypotenuse does not depend on which angle you choose. The opposite side is across from θ, and the adjacent side is next to θ. Their names depend on θ. The three ratios are:


sin θ = opposite / hypotenuse

cos θ = adjacent / hypotenuse

tan θ = opposite / adjacent

To find an angle from a ratio, use the inverse functions sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹ and tan⁻¹ on your calculator. The memory aid SOH–CAH–TOA lists the three ratios.

On the exam, check that your calculator is in degree mode, and keep unrounded values until the final answer.
examples: Find the angle θ when the hypotenuse is 10 cm and the adjacent side is 6 cm. cos θ = 6 / 10 = 0.6, so θ = cos⁻¹(0.6) ≈ 53.1°.
Find the opposite side when the hypotenuse is 8 cm and θ = 30°. Opposite side = 8 × sin 30° = 8 × 0.5 = 4 cm.
A tower is 50 m tall. You stand 80 m from its base and look at the top. The angle of elevation θ satisfies tan θ = 50 / 80 = 0.625, so θ ≈ 32°.
The angle of depression from a cliff top to a boat equals the angle of elevation from the boat to the top. These are alternate angles, because the two horizontal lines are parallel.

contrast.en: sin⁻¹ means the inverse function (arcsin), not 1 / sin. The ratios apply only to acute angles, 0° < θ < 90°, in a right-angled triangle.
contrast.ru: Запись sin⁻¹ означает обратную функцию (arcsin), а не 1 / sin. Отношения работают только для острых углов, 0° < θ < 90°, в прямоугольном треугольнике.

bearings.name: Three-figure bearings
bearings.rule:
A bearing is an angle, in degrees, measured clockwise from north at the starting point. Write it with three figures from 000° to 359°: east is 090°, south is 180° and west is 270°.

Imagine standing at the starting point and facing north. The bearing is the angle you turn to your right until you face the target. If you walk a distance d on bearing θ, you move d sin θ east and d cos θ north.

In the exam, first draw a diagram with north, the starting point and the target, then check that the angle is measured clockwise from north.
examples: The bearing of B from A is 060°. The back bearing, the bearing of A from B, is 060° + 180° = 240°.
Point Q is 5 km from P on a bearing of 110°. Put P at the origin. Then Δx = 5 sin 110° ≈ 4.70 km and Δy = 5 cos 110° ≈ −1.71 km. So Q is 4.70 km east and 1.71 km south of P.
A forward bearing of 180° has a back bearing of 000°, not 360°, because bearings run from 000° to 359°.

contrast.en: Do not confuse a bearing with the usual maths angle, which is measured from the x-axis anticlockwise. So for a bearing, the sine and cosine swap places: Δx = d sin θ, not d cos θ.
contrast.ru: Не путай азимут с обычным углом в математике: тот отсчитывают от оси x против часовой стрелки. Поэтому у азимута синус и косинус меняются местами: Δx = d sin θ, а не d cos θ.

sineCosine.name: Sine & Cosine rules (Extended)
sineCosine.rule:
In any triangle, label each side with the letter of the opposite angle: side a is opposite angle A, side b is opposite B, and side c is opposite C.


Sine rule: a / sin A = b / sin B = c / sin C

Cosine rule: a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A

Use the sine rule when you know a side and the angle opposite it. Use the cosine rule when you know two sides and the angle between them, or all three sides.

Before you choose a rule, check whether you have a matching side and opposite angle, or the angle between two known sides.
examples: In a triangle, two angles are 40° and 60°, and the side opposite 60° is 8 cm. Find the side opposite 40°: x = 8 × sin 40° / sin 60° ≈ 5.94 cm.
The sides 7 cm and 9 cm enclose an angle of 50°. Use the cosine rule: x = √(7² + 9² − 2 × 7 × 9 × cos 50°) ≈ 7.00 cm.
Cosine rule with three sides known: sides 5 cm, 6 cm and 7 cm. For the angle A opposite the 5 cm side: cos A = (6² + 7² − 5²) / (2 × 6 × 7) = 60 / 84 ≈ 0.714, so A ≈ 44.4°.

contrast.en: If you know two sides and the angle between them (SAS), you cannot use the sine rule directly; use the cosine rule. With two sides and an angle opposite one of them (SSA), there can be zero, one or two triangles.
contrast.ru: Если даны две стороны и угол между ними (SAS), теорему синусов напрямую применить нельзя: нужна теорема косинусов. Если даны две стороны и угол напротив одной из них (SSA), треугольников может быть ноль, один или два.

triangleArea.name: Area from two sides and the angle between them (Extended)
triangleArea.rule:
If a triangle has sides a and b with the angle C between them, its area is ½ab sin C. Angle C is at the vertex where sides a and b meet.

The formula comes from the usual rule, area = ½ × base × height. Take a as the base. Then the height is b sin C. The formula works for acute, right-angled and obtuse triangles.

In the exam, check that the angle lies between the two sides you use, and write the answer in square units.
examples: The angle between sides of 6 cm and 8 cm is 30°. Area = ½ × 6 × 8 × sin 30° = 24 × 0.5 = 12 cm².
An equilateral triangle with sides of 10 cm has a 60° angle between any two sides. Area = ½ × 10 × 10 × sin 60° = 25√3 ≈ 43.3 cm².

Check: in a right-angled triangle with legs 6 cm and 8 cm, the angle between the legs is 90°, and sin 90° = 1. The formula gives ½ × 6 × 8 × 1 = 24 cm². This matches the usual ½ × base × height, because the legs are the base and the height.

contrast.en: Do not forget the ½. The product ab sin C gives twice the area of the triangle.
contrast.ru: Не забудь про ½: произведение ab sin C даёт удвоенную площадь треугольника.

circleTheorems.name: Angles and tangents in a circle
circleTheorems.rule:
Circle theorems are rules that link angles and lengths in a circle. They let you find a missing angle without measuring.


The angle at the centre is twice the inscribed angle on the same arc. An inscribed angle has its vertex on the circle.

Inscribed angles on the same arc are equal.

An angle in a semicircle, subtended by a diameter, is 90°.

Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°.

A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

Two tangents drawn from the same point outside a circle have equal lengths.

Check the conditions first. Is the angle at the centre or on the circle? Is a diameter given? Are all four vertices on the circle? Does a line touch the circle at only one point?
examples: The angle at the centre is 80° and subtends arc AB. An inscribed angle on the same arc is half of it: 80° ÷ 2 = 40°.
AB is a diameter of a circle, and C is any other point on the circle. Then angle ACB = 90°, because it is an angle in a semicircle.
ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral with ∠A = 70°. Opposite angles add up to 180°, so ∠C = 180° − 70° = 110°.

review.russianTerm: Теоремы об окружностях: углы и касательные

contrast.en: Do not mix up the arcs. An angle stands on the arc between its two arms that does not contain its vertex. If the vertex lies on the minor arc, the angle stands on the major arc, so use 360° minus the minor central angle, then halve it. For a minor central angle of 80°, the angle is (360° − 80°) ÷ 2 = 140°.
contrast.ru: Не путай, на какую дугу опирается угол. Вписанный угол опирается на дугу между его сторонами, которая не содержит вершину. Если вершина лежит на меньшей дуге, угол опирается на большую дугу. Тогда используют 360° минус меньший центральный угол и делят результат на 2. При меньшем центральном угле 80° получится (360° − 80°) ÷ 2 = 140°.

sectors.name: Sectors and arcs
sectors.rule:
A sector is the part of a circle bounded by two radii and an arc.


Arc length: L = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr

Sector area: A = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr²

Perimeter of the sector: P = L + 2r

Here r is the radius (cm), θ is the central angle (°), L is the arc length (cm), A is the sector area (cm²) and P is the perimeter (cm).

Before you calculate, check the data: the radius in cm, the central angle in degrees, and whether you must find the arc length or the area.
examples: Radius 5 cm and central angle 60°. Arc length: L = (60 ÷ 360) × 2π × 5 = 5π/3 ≈ 5.24 cm. Sector area: A = (60 ÷ 360) × π × 5² = 25π/6 ≈ 13.1 cm².
An arc of length 10 cm lies on a circle of radius 4 cm. Find the central angle: θ = (10 ÷ (2π × 4)) × 360° ≈ 143.2°.

contrast.en: Do not mix up the arc and the sector. An arc is part of the circle’s boundary, so its length is measured in centimetres (cm). A sector is part of the circle’s area, so its area is measured in square centimetres (cm²). Do not put the arc-length formula where the area formula belongs.
contrast.ru: Не путай дугу и сектор. Дуга — часть окружности, её длина измеряется в сантиметрах (см). Сектор — часть круга, его площадь измеряется в квадратных сантиметрах (см²). Не подставляй формулу длины дуги вместо формулы площади.

segments.name: Area of a segment
segments.rule:
A segment (circular segment) is the region between a chord and one of its arcs. The area of the minor segment is the sector area minus the triangle area, where the triangle is formed by the chord and the two radii.

For a minor segment with radius r (cm) and central angle θ (up to 180°):


Sector area: (θ ÷ 360°) × πr²

Segment area = sector area − triangle area

Extended: the triangle area is ½r² sin θ, so the segment area = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr² − ½r² sin θ.

Before you calculate, check the radius and the central angle. Is the angle up to 180°? If it is, you are finding the minor segment, and the subtraction formula applies.
examples: Radius 6 cm and central angle 90°. Sector area: (90 ÷ 360) × π × 6² = 9π ≈ 28.27 cm². The triangle has two sides of 6 cm with a right angle between them, so its area is ½ × 6 × 6 = 18 cm². Segment area = 9π − 18 ≈ 10.27 cm².
Extended: radius 10 cm and central angle 60°. Sector area: (60 ÷ 360) × π × 10² ≈ 52.36 cm². Triangle area: ½ × 10 × 10 × sin 60° ≈ 43.30 cm². Segment area = 52.36 − 43.30 = 9.06 cm².

contrast.en: Do not give the sector area as the answer for a segment. A sector is bounded by two radii and an arc. A segment is bounded by a chord and an arc, so for a minor segment you must subtract the triangle from the sector.
contrast.ru: Не отвечай площадью сектора, если спрашивают о круговом сегменте. Сектор ограничен двумя радиусами и дугой. Круговой сегмент ограничен хордой и дугой, поэтому для меньшего кругового сегмента из площади сектора вычитают площадь треугольника.

intersectingChords.name: Intersecting chords
intersectingChords.rule:
If two chords AB and CD cross at a point P inside the circle, the product of the two parts of one chord equals the product of the two parts of the other: AP × PB = CP × PD. This is the first case of the intersecting chords theorem.

If the lines AB and CD meet at a point X outside the circle, the same formula holds, using the whole distances from X: AX × BX = CX × DX. This is the intersecting secants theorem (second case).

Check first where the chords or lines meet: inside the circle or outside it. This decides which lengths you multiply.
examples: Chords AB and CD cross at P. AP = 6 cm, PB = 4 cm and CP = 3 cm. Find PD: 6 × 4 = 3 × PD, so PD = 24 ÷ 3 = 8 cm.

Two lines meet at X outside the circle. The first line meets the circle at A and B, with AX = 4 cm and BX = 9 cm. The second line meets it at C and D, with CX = 5 cm. Find DX: 4 × 9 = 5 × DX, so DX = 36 ÷ 5 = 7.2 cm. Check: 7.2 cm is longer than 5 cm, so D is the far point, as assumed.

contrast.en: Do not confuse sum and difference. Inside the circle, AB = AP + PB, because P lies between A and B. Outside the circle, X does not lie between A and B, so AB is the difference of the distances from X to A and to B, not their sum. Multiply the distances from X; do not add them.
contrast.ru: Не путай сумму и разность. Внутри окружности AB = AP + PB, потому что P лежит между A и B. Снаружи точка X не лежит между A и B, поэтому AB — разность расстояний от X до A и до B, а не их сумма. Расстояния от X перемножай, а не складывай.

statsProb.title: Statistics and probability
statsProb.intro: On this page you choose a suitable chart for the data and draw stem-and-leaf diagrams, box plots and histograms. You also use grouped data and cumulative frequency to find typical values and spread. Extended: the standard deviation.

representation.name: Choosing a chart for the type of data
representation.rule:
Categorical data are names or groups, such as favourite colour. Numerical data are counts or measurements. Discrete data take separate values, such as 0, 1 or 2 goals. Continuous data can take any value between two limits, such as a height of 1.62 m.

A bar chart represents categorical data: its bars have equal widths, with spaces between them. A histogram represents continuous data grouped into class intervals: its bars touch. Discrete data, such as goals, are shown with a bar chart, with gaps between the bars. A line graph shows how values change in order, usually over time. A scatter diagram shows pairs of numerical values, one pair for each observation.
examples: Favourite ice cream flavour (vanilla, chocolate or mango): categorical data, so a bar chart fits.
Heights of students: continuous data, grouped into class intervals, so a histogram fits.

Goals scored in 10 matches: 0, 1, 1, 2, 0, 3, 1, 2, 0, 1. The values are discrete numbers, so a bar chart fits, with gaps between the bars: 0 goals in 3 matches, 1 goal in 4 matches, 2 goals in 2 matches and 3 goals in 1 match.
Daily temperature (°C) and portions of ice cream sold on the same days: each day gives a pair of numbers, so a scatter diagram fits.

contrast.en: A bus route number such as 12 is a label, so it is categorical data, not numerical data. Histogram class intervals have a numerical width; bar-chart categories do not.
contrast.ru: Номер маршрута 12 — это метка, поэтому такие данные качественные, а не количественные. Интервалы гистограммы имеют числовую ширину, а категории столбчатой диаграммы — нет.

stemLeaf.name: Stem-and-leaf diagrams: splitting values and reading the key
stemLeaf.rule: A stem-and-leaf diagram splits each value into a stem and a leaf. The leaf is the final digit of the value; the stem holds the other digits. Repeated values give repeated leaves. Writing the leaves in order shows how the data are spread and keeps every recorded value. The key shows the scale, for example 2|3 = 23 or 2|3 = 2.3.
examples: Back-to-back diagram comparing two classes. Class A scores are 12, 15, 17, 23 and 28; Class B scores are 11, 14, 22, 25 and 27. Class A leaves go on the left of the shared stems, Class B leaves on the right: 7 5 2 | 1 | 1 4 and 8 3 | 2 | 2 5 7. Key: 2 | 1 | 1 means 12 for Class A and 11 for Class B.

contrast.en: The stem is not always the tens digit. For the values 0.8, 1.2 and 1.5, the stem is the units digit and the leaf is the tenths digit. In a back-to-back diagram, read each side outwards from the shared stems, and state the units in the key.
contrast.ru: Стебель не всегда означает десятки. Для значений 0,8; 1,2 и 1,5 стебель — это цифра целых, а лист — цифра десятых. В двусторонней диаграмме (back-to-back diagram) читай каждую сторону от общих стеблей наружу и укажи единицы измерения в ключе.

grouped.name: Estimating the mean, median and modal class from grouped data
grouped.rule:
Grouped data show how many values fall into each class, such as 0 to 10. The exact values are lost.

Estimate the mean with the class centres: mean ≈ Σ(frequency × centre) ÷ Σ frequency. The median lies in the class that contains the middle value, but its exact value is not known. A cumulative frequency curve or interpolation gives an estimate. For classes of equal width, the modal class is the class with the highest frequency.
examples: The classes 0 < x ≤ 10, 10 < x ≤ 20 and 20 < x ≤ 30 have frequencies 4, 10 and 6, with midpoints 5, 15 and 25. The estimated mean is (5 × 4 + 15 × 10 + 25 × 6) ÷ 20 = 320 ÷ 20 = 16.
The modal class is 10 < x ≤ 20 because it has the highest frequency, 10. The 10th and 11th values out of 20 both lie in this class, so the median is also in 10 < x ≤ 20.

Half of 20 is 10, so the median is at cumulative frequency 10. Interpolate within the median class 10 < x ≤ 20: median ≈ 10 + (10 − 4) ÷ 10 × 10 = 16. Here the first 10 is the lower boundary, the 10 in brackets is half of 20, 4 is the cumulative frequency before the class, the 10 after ÷ is the class frequency and the last 10 is the class width. The exact median is not known.

contrast.en: The mode and the modal class are different. The mode is the value that occurs most often, but grouped data cannot show it; they only show the modal class. With unequal class widths, the modal class is the class with the greatest frequency per unit of class width, not the class with the greatest frequency.
contrast.ru: Мода и модальный интервал — разные понятия. Мода (mode) — значение, которое встречается чаще всего, но по сгруппированным данным её найти нельзя. По ним можно найти только модальный интервал. При разной ширине интервалов модальный интервал — тот, у которого наибольшая частота на единицу ширины, а не наибольшая частота.

sources.title: РЭШ · Сбор и группировка статистических данных

boxPlots.name: Box plots: five-point summary, quartiles and IQR
boxPlots.rule:
A box plot (box-and-whisker diagram) shows the five-point summary: the minimum, the lower quartile Q1, the median, the upper quartile Q3 and the maximum. The box spans the middle half of the data, from Q1 to Q3. Its length is the interquartile range, IQR = Q3 − Q1.

A value less than Q1 − 1.5 × IQR, or greater than Q3 + 1.5 × IQR, is an outlier. In a modified box plot, the whiskers then stop at the furthest values that are not outliers.
examples: Group A: Q1 = 8, median 12, Q3 = 16, so IQR = 16 − 8 = 8. Group B: Q1 = 7, median 9, Q3 = 10, so IQR = 10 − 7 = 3. Group A has the higher median and the wider box, so the middle half of its data is more spread out.

contrast.en: There are two whisker rules. A basic box plot from the five-point summary runs the whiskers to the minimum and maximum. In a modified box plot, the whiskers stop at the last value that is not an outlier. A value flagged as an outlier is not automatically a mistake in the data.
contrast.ru: Для усов есть два правила. В простой диаграмме размаха по пятичисловой сводке усы идут до минимума и максимума; в модифицированной диаграмме усы доходят до последнего значения, не отмеченного как выброс. Значение, отмеченное как выброс, не обязательно ошибка в данных.

model.en: Method used here: Q1 is the median of the lower half of the data and Q3 is the median of the upper half. If n is odd, leave the overall median out of both halves. Calculators and software can use other methods, so state the method you use in an exam answer.
model.ru: Здесь используется такой способ: Q1 — медиана нижней половины данных, Q3 — медиана верхней половины. Если n нечётное, медиана не входит ни в одну из половин. Калькуляторы и программы могут считать квартили иначе, поэтому в ответе на экзамене укажи, каким способом ты считаешь.

histograms.name: Histograms with equal and unequal class widths
histograms.rule:
A histogram shows frequencies of numerical data grouped into class intervals; the data can be continuous or discrete. There are no spaces between the bars. If the vertical scale shows frequency density, then bar height = frequency ÷ class width, and the area of each bar equals its frequency.

With unequal class widths, compare the areas of the bars, not their heights. A class with frequency 0 has no bar, so the histogram shows a gap there.
examples: Homework time for 110 students (minutes): 0 < t ≤ 10 has frequency 20, width 10 and frequency density 20/10 = 2; 10 < t ≤ 30 has frequency 60, width 20 and density 60/20 = 3; 30 < t ≤ 60 has frequency 30, width 30 and density 30/30 = 1.
Frequency = density × width, so the total is 2 × 10 + 3 × 20 + 1 × 30 = 20 + 60 + 30 = 110 students. The areas of the bars add up to 110.

contrast.en: When class widths are unequal, the height of a bar is not its frequency: a bar of height 2 and width 10 has frequency 20 (its area), not 2.
contrast.ru: При разной ширине интервалов высота столбца — не частота: столбец высотой 2 и шириной 10 имеет частоту 20 (его площадь), а не 2.

caption.en: These bars have different heights but the same frequency; height is frequency density.
caption.ru: Высоты различаются, но частоты одинаковы; высота задаёт плотность частоты.

cumulativeFreq.name: Cumulative frequency graphs: reading medians, quartiles and percentiles
cumulativeFreq.rule: Cumulative frequency is the running total of frequencies up to a value. For grouped data, plot each running total at the upper boundary of its class, starting at 0 at the lower boundary of the first class. The curve never decreases. To find the p-th percentile, find the value at cumulative frequency (p/100) × N, where N is the total frequency. If this point lies inside a class, estimate the value by straight-line interpolation between the two boundaries of that class.
examples: Intervals 0 < x ≤ 10, 10 < x ≤ 20 and 20 < x ≤ 30 have frequencies 4, 10 and 6. The running totals are 4, 14 and 20, so plot (0, 0), (10, 4), (20, 14) and (30, 20).

With N = 20, use straight-line interpolation to estimate the values. The median is at cumulative frequency 10: median ≈ 16. Q1 is at cumulative frequency 5: Q1 ≈ 11. Q3 is at cumulative frequency 15: Q3 ≈ 21.67 (to 2 d.p.).
90th percentile: cumulative frequency 0.9 × 20 = 18. Interpolating between (20, 14) and (30, 20): x = 20 + (18 − 14)/(20 − 14) × 10 = 26.67 (to 2 d.p.).

contrast.en: The curve does not have to be S-shaped; its shape depends on the data. A flat part means that class has frequency 0, so the cumulative frequency does not rise there. Never divide by that zero when you interpolate.
contrast.ru: График не обязан быть S-образным: его форма зависит от данных. Горизонтальный участок означает, что частота этого интервала равна 0, поэтому накопленная частота там не растёт. При интерполяции нельзя делить на эту нулевую частоту.

model.en: Straight-line interpolation assumes that values are spread evenly within each class; the exact individual values are not known.
model.ru: Линейная интерполяция предполагает, что значения внутри каждого интервала распределены равномерно. Точные значения неизвестны.

stdDev.name: Standard deviation: measuring spread from the mean (Extended)
stdDev.rule: Standard deviation (σ) measures how far the values typically lie from the mean, in the same units as the data. For n values with mean x̄: σ = √(Σ(x − x̄)²/n), where Σ(x − x̄)² is the sum of the squared deviations from the mean. The variance is σ².
examples: Data: 2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9, so n = 8 and the mean is 40/8 = 5. Deviations from the mean: −3, −1, −1, −1, 0, 0, 2, 4. Squared: 9, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 4, 16, with sum 32. So σ = √(32/8) = √4 = 2.
Compare with the data above: 4.5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5.5 also has mean 5. Its squared deviations sum to 0.5, so σ = √(0.5/6) ≈ 0.289. The values lie much closer to the mean, so the spread is smaller.

contrast.en: Variance is in squared units (for example, cm²), so compare spreads with the standard deviation, which is in the original units (cm). A standard deviation of 0 means that all the values are equal.
contrast.ru: Дисперсия измеряется в квадратных единицах (например, см²), поэтому разброс сравнивают по стандартному отклонению, которое измеряется в исходных единицах (см). Стандартное отклонение, равное 0, означает, что все значения одинаковы.

sources.title: РЭШ · Дисперсия и среднее квадратичное отклонение

pieCharts.name: Pie charts: reading sectors and calculating angles
pieCharts.rule: A pie chart shows how one whole is split into non-overlapping categories. Each category gets a sector. Its sector angle is 360° × f/N, where f is the frequency of the category and N is the total frequency. The angles of all the sectors add up to 360°, which is 100% of the whole.
examples: A survey of 60 people on how they travel: 20 walk, 10 cycle and 30 drive. Angles: walk 20/60 × 360° = 120°; cycle 10/60 × 360° = 60°; drive 30/60 × 360° = 180°. The three angles add up to 360°.
A pie chart of 240 students has a 30° sector for 'cycle'. The number who cycle is (30/360) × 240 = 20 students.

contrast.en: A sector shows a share of the whole, so you need the total to turn it into a count. A pie chart works only if the categories do not overlap and make up one whole: multiple-choice answers can add up to more than 100%.
contrast.ru: Сектор показывает долю целого, поэтому, чтобы получить количество, нужен общий итог. Круговая диаграмма подходит, только если категории не пересекаются и составляют одно целое: при множественном выборе ответы могут в сумме дать больше 100%.
